newsitem.title: GERMANY: Meeting on Zaire military role postponed - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: Meeting on Zaire military role postponed - Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday a meeting to discuss a possible military component for an international rescue mission to Zaire had been postponed to Friday.
"A meeting was due to take place in Stuttgart today... that has now been postponed until the day after tomorrow," Kinkel told reporters in Bonn.

Kinkel said some countries which had originally agreed to take part in a military mission were now unsure whether it was still necessary. He said Germany would not say anything on the matter as it would not be sending troops.
"A political meeting will first be held in New York to decide if a military force should be sent and how it would look," he said.
Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien had already said the Stuttgart meeting would probably be delayed until Friday. The political meeting was due to take place on Wednesday.
Kinkel said it was vital the international community continued to provide as much humanitarian help as possible, regardless of any decision about a military mission to Central Africa.
